newsitem.title: CANADA: GOLF-MARSHALL FIGHTS OFF MIGRAINE TO SHARE LEAD IN CANADA.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-MARSHALL FIGHTS OFF MIGRAINE TO SHARE LEAD IN CANADA.

text.p: Scotland's Kathryn Marshall came close to quitting after 15 holes due to feeling ill, but she stayed the course to share the lead after the first round of the LPGA du Maurier golf tournament Thursday.
Marshall, playing with a wet towel wrapped around her neck to fight off a migraine headache, shot a five-under-par 68 to share the lead with Americans Colleen Walker and Vicki Fergon.
"Whenever I do play well I tend to get headaches," she said. "When you're not well you concentrate on each shot more. You just want to get off the course."
Marshall, from Dundee, Scotland, shot 33 in the front nine and 35 while in obvious pain on the back nine.
Walker had two 34s and Fergon shot a 33 and 35.
Eight golfers were at 69 trailing the leaders by one shot.
"I thought I'd be sick on the course, I was shaking," Marshall said. "It started on the fourth hole and it was just survival after that.
"It got to the point where I wasn't even looking at the putt. I was looking for shade."
Marshall has one career victory on the Tour, in 1995, and was two shots away from her best round ever.
While Marshall suffered, Walker revelled in her own success.
"Everything worked today," Walker said. "I've been working really hard on my putting and I finally made some today."
Last year's winner Laura Davies of Britain and 1997 Tour leader Annika Sorenstam, who has four victories this year, finished the day at even par.
